I cannot recommend a surgical approach or treatment plan for your patient—those decisions belong to your treating clinical team. I can show you the available measurements from the cadaveric dataset and explain what they mean in the literature, which may help inform your discussion with the surgical team.

**Available data (cadaveric specimen ZETA only):**

| Measurement | Value | Reference range [Zahara2019] | Status |
|-------------|-------|------------------------------|--------|
| Cochlear A (diameter) | 8.97 mm | 8.17–9.33 mm | In range [S8] |
| Cochlear B (width) | 6.81 mm | 5.73–7.50 mm | In range [S9] |
| Cochlear height | 4.36 mm | 2.80–3.72 mm | Out of range [S10] |
| Facial nerve → scala tympani distance | 1.18 mm | — | [S12] |
| Chorda tympani → scala tympani distance | 3.65 mm | — | [S14] |

**What these measurements mean:**

- **Cochlear A, B, height** are derived from the oriented bounding box of the **scala tympani**, a landmark-free proxy method used because the dataset's "Scala Vestibuli" label includes the vestibule and semicircular canals [S5][S17].
- **A (8.97 mm)** is used to estimate cochlear duct length and therefore electrode length in clinical practice [Schurzig2018, Breitsprecher2022].
- The **height value (4.36 mm)** is outside the published reference range; this is a QC warning, not an error [S10].
- **Distances** to the facial nerve and chorda tympani matter for surgical risk assessment [Noble2008] [D6].

**Important limitations:**

- This data comes from a single cadaveric specimen (ZETA), not from your patient.
- The cochlear dimensions are a proxy method; classical definitions use anatomical landmarks (round window, modiolar axis) which are not available here [S5].
- CochleaHub is a research tool on cadaveric data: it explains measurements, it does not recommend treatment for a patient [S2].

**Next steps:**

Discuss these measurements with your surgical team. They can use the cochlear A value (8.97 mm) along with clinical judgment and additional imaging to estimate electrode length and plan the surgical approach.
